title: Observability onboarding brief for new ops curators
content:
Purpose

This brief is a compact, practical onboarding guide for new "ops curators" on the Observability team. Ops curators are responsible for curating dashboards, owning lightweight probes, triaging first-line inference incidents, and stewarding metric & trace hygiene for ML rollouts. The doc collects pragmatic checklists, naming/definition rules, sampling heuristics, and quick runbook snippets — intentionally short and task-oriented.

Audience and scope
- Audience: new engineers joining eng-observability in the first 30–90 days.
- Scope: token-inference pipelines (hosted / dedicated / private), KV cache and batching paths, model routing & fallbacks, tenant-aware dashboards.

First 30 days — high priority checklist
1) Read: Top 3 canonical pages (link in linked_artifacts). Skim the rollout telemetry contract doc.
2) Access: Gain read/write to Grafana dashboards and probe repo. Verify IAM for tracing span redaction.
3) Observe: Run the "operator quickcard" playbook during an oncall shadow shift (pair with a rotation owner).
4) Curate: Pick one dashboard with >50% query cost and propose a slimming patch (remove redundant panel / add coarse aggregation).
5) Probe: Adopt an existing synthetic probe, deploy a small variant and confirm alerts fire in the sandbox.

Metric definition style guide (short form)
- Format: <domain>.<measure>.<aggregation?> e.g. inference.request.count, inference.latency.p95, kvcache.hit_rate.
- Unit explicitness: include unit in comments (ms, tokens, ratio).
- Owner tag: every metric must have an owners tag in the metric metadata (team/email).
- Dimensions allowed: model, region, deployment_type, route, tenant_bucket (not PII).

Canonical metrics to know (examples)
- inference.request.count — incoming API requests (route-level). Unit: requests. Primary dimensions: route, model, region.
- inference.tokens.generated.sum — tokens produced across responses. Unit: tokens. Useful for billing/cost attribution.
- inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 — end-to-end TTF token or TTF-first-token depending on panel. Unit: ms.
- kvcache.hit_rate — fraction of prefix lookup hits (0..1). Unit: ratio.
- batcher.aggregate.size.mean — mean request batch size entering the GPU pipeline. Unit: requests.
- host.gpu.utilization.percent — per-host GPU utilization (30s rollup).
- tenant.session.warmth_index — heuristic for cache warmth per tenant (derived, see notes).

Tracing conventions and quick heuristics
- Span naming: prefer short, stable names using component.action, e.g. http.request, batcher.aggregate, kvcache.fetch, model.decode, model.load.
- Span tags (attributes): model.name, model.version, deployment.kind (hosted|dedicated|private), tenant_bucket, route, rollout_id (when testing).
- Sampling: default reservoir 1% of requests, always-sample requests with: errors (status >= 500), latency > p99, high token count (> 10k), or explicit debug header.
- Privacy: PII must never be logged in attributes. Use hashed or bucketed tenant ids if necessary. Redact prompt text unless explicit customer consent and secure storage is in place.
- Trace stitching: include request_id and session_id in the top-level span and as a tag on key downstream spans to ease reconstruction.

Dashboard hygiene rules (practical)
- Query budget: each dashboard should aim to be <= 5 second-CPU per refresh (dashboard owner responsible).
- Panel cost labels: add a small note under expensive panels showing estimated query cost and last-run time range.
- Cardinality control: avoid panels with unbounded tag grouping (e.g., tenant_id); use tenant_bucket or top-N + "other" bucketing.
- Alert granularity: prefer route/model-level alerts for regressions. Use cohort-SLIs when needing per-tenant signals.
- Deprecation: annotate panels with a deprecation date when replacing or consolidating.

Probe lifecycle and runbook snippets
- Probe types: synthetic (canary), smoke (startup checks), regression probes (prompt sets).
- Deployment: probe configs live in telemetry/probes. Test locally -> deploy to sandbox -> enable sample mode -> promote.
- Runbook snippet: If inference.latency.p95 spikes > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes: 1) Check model load errors in traces, 2) Inspect batcher.aggregate.size.mean and kvcache.hit_rate, 3) Roll forward to alternative variant (rollout_id tag), 4) If GPU saturation present, shift traffic to dedicated fallback pool.

Small example: creating a compact token-economics panel
- Panels: tokens.generated.sum (per route) + cost_per_token * tokens.generated -> shows daily spend by route.
- Use a 6 panel layout: (1) qps, (2) latency p95, (3) tokens/day, (4) kvcache hit_rate, (5) batch size mean, (6) cost estimate. Keep timeframe toggles defaulted to 1h / 1d.

Ownership and handoffs
- Each dashboard must list a single owner + two reviewers. Owners are responsible for query cost and alert definitions.
- Handoffs: when a feature team creates new panels, they must tag the panel with the feature name and create a rollout telemetry ticket (JIRA) linking probes and alerts.

Common mistakes new curators make
- Leaving high-cardinality group_by with tenant_id.
- Not including rollout_id in traces during canaries.
- Alerts that only trigger on raw counts (use normalized rates or p95 windows).
- Overly chatty span attributes (extra baggage causing storage blowup).

Practical workshop: 2-hour session outline for week 2
- 0–15m: Quick intro to our metric naming and trace schema.
- 15–45m: Guided walk-through of a noisy dashboard; propose slimming edits.
- 45–90m: Hands-on: implement one probe change and deploy to sandbox.
- 90–120m: Pair with oncall to watch probe fire and read traces.

Outstanding questions and TODOs
- Should we standardize tenant_bucket definitions across teams? (ACTION: propose canonical buckets by 2026-02-01).
- Decide permanent default trace sampling ratio for hosted vs private deployments (current default is 1%).
- Create a compact "cost estimate" library for panels to avoid ad-hoc cost calculations.

Notes to self / quick links
- Confluence onboarding page (linked_artifacts).
- Probe repo (linked_artifacts).
- Typical Jira epic to reference: JIRA-OBS-342 (instrumentation sprint).

If you're new: ping @Ethan for pairing on your first dashboard patch, and @Lina for trace redaction approvals. Welcome aboard — this team cares about fast, actionable signals and pragmatic ownership.
